candidates.summary: Object equality depends on the pointer's static type, so one object yields unequal Objects and the docs' 'comparable and safe as a map key' / 'equal iff they name the same object' fails
candidates.failure_scenario: A persisted tok := &Token{} read as reflect.Of(tok), reflect.Of((*Alias)(tok)) with type Alias Token, and reflect.Of((*struct{ n int })(tok)) gives three Objects with one Address() but Type() 'b3eq.Token', 'b3eq.Alias' and '', because declaredTypeName reads tv.T (the pointer's type) rather than the heap item's own value type. a == b and a == c are false and a map[reflect.Object]bool takes three entries for one object. A realm deduping or registering objects by Object, as docs/resources/gno-stdlibs.md:740 and the ADR line 80 invite, admits the same object again under each pointer type, with ok true every time. Inference, not run: a caller in another realm can do the same with type Alias victim.Token, since the conversion only needs identical underlying types. Fix: take typ from the heap item's own TypedValue (hiv.Value.T) in X_objectInfo, which also makes the type P *Token unwrap unnecessary.

candidates.summary: The foreign-finalize filetest never reaches touchForeignRealm: 'theirs' is a package var, stamped by this realm at package load before SetFooer runs
candidates.failure_scenario: The PR body and the author's reply to clockworkgr say this test covers the touchForeignRealm branch of assignNewObjectID (realm.go:2036-2038). But theirs = &fooer{n: 2} is a package-level var, and package-level objects are already stamped when main starts (zrealm_reflect_identity.gno prints an address for its package var 'standalone' on main's first line). So crossrealm.SetFooer(cross(cur), theirs) at line 36 hands over an already-finalized object, assignNewObjectID never runs for it, and the Output is identical whether that branch takes the tick from the creating realm or the persisting one. The duplicate-address regression the test header describes goes uncaught. Fix: allocate theirs inside main before SetFooer.

candidates.summary: 'PkgPath is the realm that created the object' is false for adopted objects: the VM re-stamps their PkgID to the persisting realm, so PkgPath names a realm that did not create them
candidates.failure_scenario: assignNewObjectID (realm.go:1995-2027) re-stamps PkgID to the finalizing realm for an object with a zero PkgID (allocated outside a realm context), an ephemeral /e/<addr>/run PkgID (gnokey maketx run), or a stdlib PkgID. A user's maketx run script that builds &foo.Token{...} (the StructValue keeps foo's PkgID by type-driven stamping, the heap item takes the run PkgID) and hands it to r/foo gets it adopted, after which Of(tok).PkgPath() == "gno.land/r/foo" and Type() == "gno.land/r/foo.Token", the same answer as a Token r/foo minted itself. The ADR section 3 presents PkgPath as answering 'which realm created this'. Unrun: the filetest harness treats /e/ as non-realm and rejects cross there. Fix: describe PkgPath as the realm whose clock minted the identity and which owns the object, as reflect.gno:179 half does.
candidates.verify_by: txtar under gno.land/pkg/integration/testdata: add a realm r/foo with an exported Token type and a crossing Register(cur realm, t *Token) that stores t; gnokey maketx run a script doing foo.Register(cross, &foo.Token{}); then a call in r/foo printing reflect.Of(stored).PkgPath(). Expect gno.land/r/foo although the run script created it

candidates.summary: HasIdentity is true for a bound method value or method expression that no realm boundary will ever stamp, so the documented 'not yet, ask again after the boundary' never resolves
candidates.failure_scenario: With tok persisted, reflect.Of(tok.Method) and reflect.Of((*Token).Method) both return ok false and HasIdentity true. Each evaluation of tok.Method allocates a fresh BoundMethodValue that is never persisted unless stored, so every later call gives the same answer. A realm following the docs (gno-stdlibs.md:777, reflect.gno:70-74: retry after the boundary, or refuse and split the work across two calls) retries or refuses forever. The docs table only promises true/true for a stored bound method, so this is a semantics gap and not a wrong address.
candidates.verify_by: Filetest with a persisted tok := &Token{} and func (t *Token) Method(): print reflect.Of(tok.Method) ok and reflect.HasIdentity(tok.Method), in main and again after a crossing call returns. Expect 'ok: false has: true' in both
candidates.evidence: Probe run at head (scratch filetest, not kept): 'tok.Method fresh ok: false has: true pkg:  type:' and '(*Token).Method ok: false has: true pkg:  type:', while 'bm stored ok: true has: true' for the same bound method kept in a package var

candidates.summary: The consensus preimage is objectid:RID<UPPERHEX>:<n> through PkgID.String(), not objectid:<ID()>, so an address cannot be recomputed from the ID() spelling the docs offer for storage dumps
candidates.failure_scenario: DeriveObjectCryptoAddr hashes "objectid:" + oid.PkgID.String() + ":" + NewTime (misc.go:222). PkgID.String() is fmt.Sprintf("RID%X", ...) (realm.go:75), while Object.ID() and the store key use MarshalAmino's lowercase hex with no prefix (ownership.go:48). An indexer following the ADR's 'derived by hashing objectid:<pkgid>:<newtime>' and the docs' 'ID ... for matching against a storage dump' computes sha256("objectid:" + ID()) and gets a different address for every object. The ADR should state the exact bytes, since it calls the layout consensus state.
